'''María Fernanda Ceriani''' is an Argentine biologist. She studies the neuronal mechanisms involved in the regulation of [[circadian rhythm]]s, using ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]]'' as a biological model. She is the president of INIS Biotech, heads the Behavioral Genetics Laboratory at the [[Leloir Institute|Leloir Institute Foundation]], and is a researcher with the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council]] (CONICET). Ceriani received her PhD from the [[University of Buenos Aires]] and did postdoctoral research at the [[Scripps Research Institute]]. She won a [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Award]] in 2011.

==Early life and education==
María Fernanda Ceriani was born on 26 May 1966 in [[Ramos Mejía]], Argentina.<ref name="Konex">{{cite web |title=María Fernanda Ceriani |url=https://www.fundacionkonex.org/b4548-maria-fernanda-ceriani |publisher=Fundación Konex |access-date=8 August 2023 |language=es}}</ref> She graduated from the Escuela Nacional Normal Superior Manuel Dorrego in 1983. Ceriani attended the [[Faculty of Exact and Natural Sciences]] of the [[University of Buenos Aires]], earning her [[Master of Science|MSc]] in biology in 1990 and a PhD in biological sciences in 1996.<ref name="EMBO"/> She started her doctorate with Esteban Hopp at the Institute of Biotechnology of the [[National Agricultural Technology Institute]] in [[Castelar]],<ref name="QuímicaViva">{{cite journal |last1=Petrera |first1=Erina |issue=17 |title=Entrevista Dra. Maria Fernanda Ceriani |url=http://www.quimicaviva.qb.fcen.uba.ar/v17n3/E0141.htm |volume=3 |journal=QuímicaViva |issn=1666-7948 |language=es |date=September 2018}}</ref> and continued research in [[Roger N. Beachy]]'s laboratory at [[Scripps Research]] in [[La Jolla]], California. She was a postdoctoral fellow at Scripps Research, working in the laboratory of chronobiologist [[Steve A. Kay]] from 1997 to 2002. She then returned to Argentina, where she was selected in a contest to repatriate researchers to start a laboratory at the Leloir Institute Foundation.<ref name="EMBO"/>

==Scientific career==
Ceriani studies the neuronal mechanisms involved in the regulation of [[circadian rhythm]]s. She principally works with ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]]'' as a biological model and employs behavioral experiments and [[immunohistochemistry]].<ref name="QuímicaViva"/> She has authored papers with [[Michael Rosbash]]<ref name="EMBO"/> and has written about circadian [[Behavioral plasticity|plasticity]] in ''[[Drosophila]]''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Frenkel |first1=Lia |last2=Ceriani |first2=María Fernanda |title=Recent Advances in the Use of Drosophila in Neurobiology and Neurodegeneration |date=2011 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-387003-2 |pages=107–130 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=b0p0t6DSqIUC&q=ceriani&pg=PA107 |language=en}}</ref>

Ceriani is the president of INIS Biotech, the technology liaison office of [[Leloir Institute]], and has headed the Behavioral Genetics Laboratory at the Leloir Institute Foundation since 2002. She is also a researcher with the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council]] (CONICET) and has membership in the Latin American Academy of Sciences as of 2019.<ref name="infobae"/> In 2021, she was appointed a member of [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] as principal investigator of the Institute for Biochemical Research at CONICET.<ref name="EMBO">{{cite web |title=Fernanda Ceriani fue incorporada a la Organización Europea de Biología Molecular (EMBO) |url=https://www.conicet.gov.ar/fernanda-ceriani-fue-incorporada-a-la-organizacion-europea-de-biologia-molecular-embo/ |publisher=Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas |language=es |date=8 June 2021}}</ref>

Ceriani received the national [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Award]] in 2011.<ref name="infobae">{{cite news |title=Las damas de la ciencia argentina galardonadas: ocho reconocidas científicas que trabajan en la lucha contra el coronavirus |url=https://www.infobae.com/salud/ciencia/2020/10/28/las-damas-de-la-ciencia-argentina-galardonadas-ocho-reconocidas-cientificas-que-trabajan-en-la-lucha-contra-el-coronavirus/ |work=infobae |date=28 October 2020|lang=es}}</ref> She received a [[Konex Award]] in 2013.<ref name="Konex"/>

Ceriani's laboratory received funding from the [[National Institutes of Health]] in 2020 for a research collaboration with universities in California and Washington to describe structural changes of clock neurons that regulate the circadian rhythms in the brains of mice and ''Drosophila'' flies.<ref name="EMBO"/> Following the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina|COVID-19 pandemic]], Ceriani was part of a group of researchers from CONICET studying the impact of [[social isolation]] on [[circadian rhythm]]s in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Equipo de investigación lanza una aplicación para mejorar el descanso |url=https://www.argentina.gob.ar/noticias/equipo-de-investigacion-lanza-una-aplicacion-para-mejorar-el-descanso |publisher=Argentina.gob.ar |date=2 September 2021 |lang=es}}</ref> She was a project leader in the development of ''Mi Reloj Interno'', an app for monitoring the rhythms.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lanzan versión iOS de una app gratuita para cuidar el reloj biológico |url=https://www.agenciacyta.org.ar/2021/12/lanzan-version-ios-de-una-app-gratuita-para-cuidar-el-reloj-biologico/ |work=Agencia CyTA |date=9 December 2021|lang=es}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ceriani has three children, two of whom are twins.<ref name="QuímicaViva"/>
